backlog.title: admissionSystemType is never populated by either real production caller of computeAdmissionOutlook
backlog.current_behavior: lib/admissions/persist.ts:36-39 and lib/universities/counseling-adapter.ts:342-346 both call computeAdmissionOutlook with only {profileStrength, admissionRate, dataConfidence} -- admissionSystemType is never passed. Per outlook.ts's own contract this defaults to holistic-style classification for every call.
evidence: lib/admissions/outlook.ts:42,51-53,85,90,113-115 (feature definition and default-to-holistic contract)
lib/admissions/persist.ts:36-39 (production caller #1, field omitted)
lib/universities/counseling-adapter.ts:342-346 (production caller #2, field omitted)
git grep across origin/main for admissionSystemType/credential_gate: only outlook.ts, its test file, and these two callers match -- no Gate-1 lookup exists anywhere
backlog.correct_behavior: A target whose admissions system is credential/exam-gated (per RULE-ADMISSIONS country research) should surface outlook: 'not_applicable', not a reach/competitive/likely classification with a numeric estimate range.
backlog.why_it_matters: Every student targeting every university in every country currently gets holistic framing regardless of actual target-system type. This is not a partial or approximate effect -- the built, tested feature has zero live impact today. Directly the kind of 'confidently wrong answer' the assignment asked to prioritize.
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Build the Gate-1 lookup design spec section 7 item 1 already calls for (currently unbuilt anywhere), then thread its result into both call sites as admissionSystemType. universities.application_system (already a live column: UCAS/Common App/Studielink/Parcoursup/OSYM-YKS/uni-assist/direct) is a plausible existing input signal, though see GAP-002 on why country/platform alone is insufficient.
backlog.confidence: high -- confirmed by direct code read and exhaustive grep, not inferred

backlog.title: No field-existence check -- RULE-ADMISSIONS-021 (Medicine/Law not undergraduate objects in US/Canada) is unrepresented anywhere checked
backlog.current_behavior: outlook.ts takes no field/programme parameter at all. A student who sets an undergraduate target university with intended field Medicine or Law in the US (or Law in Canada outside the narrow Quebec CEGEP route) would receive a full outlook computation as if the target were real.
evidence: lib/admissions/outlook.ts:44-53 (AdmissionOutlookInputs has no field/programme-level input at all)
docs/research/admissions-systems/program-requirements/medicine.json, country_key=united_states/canada, mechanism_type='not_available_at_undergraduate_level' (medicine.md's own term)
docs/research/admissions-systems/program-requirements/law.json, country_key=united_states, mechanism_type='not_available_at_undergraduate_level'
backlog.correct_behavior: A field-existence check upstream of outlook computation should produce a distinct message ('this isn't offered as an undergraduate degree in this country at all') rather than any reach/competitive/likely-shaped answer, including not_applicable (which currently means 'no activity review', a different claim).
backlog.why_it_matters: The clearest case in this analysis of the product answering a question that has no valid answer as posed, rather than surfacing an honest unknown -- directly contradicts this package's own product mandate (never present a nonexistent target as evaluable).
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: A field-existence table keyed on (country, field) at minimum (Medicine, Law for now; extensible), consulted before or alongside outlook computation. Needs its own outlook/message state distinct from not_applicable per GAP-001.
backlog.confidence: high for the finding that no such check exists in the 4 checked files; not verified whether target-university/field capture elsewhere in the app has any validation of this (out of this pass's scope)

backlog.title: Gate-1 as specified is binary; real country data shows at least three shapes
backlog.current_behavior: outlook.ts's admissionSystemType is a 2-value enum (holistic | credential_gate); the design spec's Gate-1 is likewise framed as yes/no.
evidence: lib/admissions/outlook.ts:42 (2-value AdmissionSystemType)
docs/research/counseling-intelligence/18-geography-conditional-scoring-design-spec.md section 2

docs/research/admissions-systems/README.md RULE-ADMISSIONS-001 (Netherlands/Italy non-selective: eligible functionally equals admitted, no ranking/competition at all -- distinct from Turkey/Ireland's real-but-opaque-to-ORYN ranking)
backlog.correct_behavior: Distinguish at minimum: (a) holistic review happens, (b) centralized algorithmic score-rank placement (real competition exists, ORYN can't see the cutoff), (c) threshold/qualification-eligibility with no competition once met.
backlog.why_it_matters: outlook.ts's single static notApplicableReason string is worded around 'credential/exam-gated' -- accurate for Turkey/Ireland-shape systems, actively misleading for Dutch/Italian open-programme admission, which isn't exam-gated in any sense a student would recognize.
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Widen AdmissionSystemType to at least 3 values before the Gate-1 lookup (GAP-000) is built, not patched afterward. Each value needs its own message template.

backlog.title: Gate-1 keyed by target country alone cannot represent applicant-pathway bifurcation
backlog.current_behavior: Design spec section 1's signal table keys geography off target_universities -> university_id -> universities.country -- one value per target, no applicant-type/pathway dimension.
evidence: docs/research/counseling-intelligence/18-geography-conditional-scoring-design-spec.md section 1 (signal table)
RULE-ADMISSIONS-013 (Hong Kong JUPAS/non-JUPAS; France Parcoursup/DAP)
RULE-ADMISSIONS-014 (Ireland CAO vs. non-EU-direct -- structurally opposite evidence models in one country)
RULE-ADMISSIONS-017 (Turkey's own domestic-vs-foreign-national split, by schooling location not nationality)
backlog.correct_behavior: Gate-1 lookup keyed on (target country, applicant pathway) where pathway is derived from the student's own citizenship/schooling-location relative to the target country -- not the target country alone, and not the student's own country alone either (the design spec's existing section 6 warning covers the latter, not this).
backlog.why_it_matters: A Turkish student targeting France needs DAP framing (no essay field, 3-choice cap, TCF gate); a French Bac holder targeting the same country needs Parcoursup framing (essay sometimes present, 10-choice cap, no language test). Country-only keying gives both students the same answer.
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Add a pathway dimension to the Gate-1 key, derived from profiles.citizenship_countries / schooling-location fields already in schema (per counseling lane's own migration 0047 note) crossed against target country.
backlog.confidence: high for the country-only-key limitation as specified; the exact pathway-derivation logic is a design task not attempted here

backlog.title: Field-override layer needs an institution dimension, not just (country, field)
backlog.current_behavior: Design spec section 7 item 3 proposes a field-specific override layer keyed on (target country, target field).
evidence: docs/research/counseling-intelligence/18-geography-conditional-scoring-design-spec.md section 7 item 3
RULE-ADMISSIONS-018/019 (NUS: zero test/interview across all 10 core Engineering majors, test required for Architecture in the same college)

docs/research/admissions-systems/program-requirements/architecture.json, country_key=ireland finding: TU Dublin bakes portfolio into initial CAO points, UCD does not -- same country, same CAO 'Restricted' flag
docs/research/admissions-systems/program-requirements/architecture.json, country_key=switzerland finding: ETH Zurich Architecture requires zero architecture-specific evidence
backlog.correct_behavior: Override table keyed on (country, institution, field), or an explicit institution-overrides-field-default layer.
backlog.why_it_matters: A (country, field) key gets country-level and most field-level distinctions right but cannot represent same-country-same-field institution variance, which this pass found to be real and sometimes larger than the country-level or field-level signal alone.
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Widen the design spec's proposed key by one dimension before implementation begins.

backlog.title: CourseLevel enum has no value for non-AP/IB/A-Level rigor
backlog.current_behavior: RIGOR_WEIGHT in both lib/requirements/evaluate.ts and lib/scoring/dimensions/academics.ts covers only ap/ib_hl/a_level/dual_enrollment (weight 1), ib_sl (0.75), honors (0.5), regular/other (0). No value represents e.g. a Turkish Fen Lisesi advanced track, or Turkey's OBP diploma-grade mechanic.

lib/requirements/evaluate.ts:8-17 (same enum reused)

backlog.correct_behavior: Not specified here (schema design, out of this pass's scope) -- flagged as higher-priority now given new corroborating evidence, not as a new discovery.

backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Not attempted here -- the existing in-code comment already names the fix shape (new CourseLevel enum value + migration).

backlog.title: Opportunity profile-need scoring doesn't condition on the student's target system's Gate-1 status
backlog.current_behavior: computeProfileNeedScore in lib/opportunities/matching.ts:191-195 scores an opportunity as high-need (85) whenever it addresses a student's weakest profile dimension, with no awareness of whether that dimension has any channel into the student's actual target admissions system.
evidence: lib/opportunities/matching.ts:191-195

RULE-ADMISSIONS-021 sibling finding: leadership/community_impact/entrepreneurship/research/awards_distinction have zero channel into YKS placement (confirmed independently by this package's Turkey research and the counseling lane's RULE-COUNSEL-057/109)
backlog.correct_behavior: Not necessarily a hard suppression -- the opportunity may still be worthwhile for general development or a different target -- but the 'profile need' framing implicitly suggests admissions relevance that may not hold for a Gate-1-no target.
backlog.why_it_matters: Secondary and not a wrong answer today (opportunities remain genuinely useful for development regardless), but the same Gate-1 concept recurring unaddressed in a second subsystem is worth tracking alongside the primary outlook gaps.
backlog.proposed_fix_shape: Once Gate-1 exists (GAP-000), consider whether computeProfileNeedScore's messaging (not necessarily its numeric score) should distinguish 'closes an admissions-relevant gap' from 'good for development, not admissions-relevant for your current target'.
backlog.confidence: medium -- the underlying Gate-1 concept and its absence here are both confirmed; whether this rises to product-worthy priority is a judgment call, not a fact

not_flagged_as_gaps.reason: Very likely correct by design -- the design spec's own section 5 and this product's own non-negotiable #11 (career profile score is different from admissions probability) both argue development scoring should stay geography-independent while admissions outlook is a separate, geography-conditional layer. Recorded so a future pass doesn't mistake this for an oversight.
Different domain from university-admissions evaluation -- none of the 21 RULE-ADMISSIONS-* rules govern opportunity eligibility directly. Confirmed as mostly orthogonal, not silently broken.
